title: China cuts margin requirement to 80% in fresh market support push, but will it work?
body: The margin cut may help mainland sentiment at the open, especially in the high-beta growth names on ChiNext and the STAR board, where leveraged retail money tends to concentrate. Because the change only takes effect on 30 November, its direct flow impact is a week away, so traders may treat early gains as anticipatory and easy to reverse. Hong Kong-listed Chinese tech is outside the scope of the measures and stays more exposed to the global AI rout. The yuan is unlikely to react much unless the measures bring clear inflows back into mainland equities. ---- Earlier: Seoul readies a market fund unused since 2008 after the Kospi sinks --- Beijing is making it cheaper to borrow to buy stocks, but with margin balances already shrinking, the real shortage looks like confidence, not credit. Summary: China's three main exchanges will lower the minimum margin requirement for buying stocks on credit to 80% from 100%, effective 30 November, with CSRC approval. The move reverses a January tightening and applies to both new and existing contracts. Margin loans have fallen by more than 20% since late June, to about 2.2 trillion yuan. Chinese media estimate the change could free up close to 400 billion yuan. The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges and the national clearing house announced fee cuts, and Shenzhen proposed market makers for ChiNext. The steps follow a broader 2 November support package after mainland stocks' worst month in a decade.

title: Australia flash PMI sinks to 46.1 as private sector shrinks at fastest pace in 5 years
body: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external demand, at a time when global equities are already under heavy pressure. Prices are still running above their long-run averages, though, so policymakers are unlikely to move quickly to declare inflation beaten. Traders may also treat the flash reading cautiously until the final data in early December. --- Higher interest rates are now hitting Australian demand across the board: services have joined manufacturing in contraction, new orders are at a five-year low and confidence is draining away. Summary: Australia's flash composite PMI fell to 46.1 in November from 48.2, the lowest since August 2021 and a second month in contraction. Services activity slid to 46.2 from 48.5, and the manufacturing PMI eased to 48.7 from 49.6. New orders fell at the fastest pace since August 2021, with services new business falling faster than manufacturing. Export orders fell at the sharpest rate in just over two years. Firms cut staff and cleared backlogs, and business confidence hit a three-year low. Input cost and selling price inflation both eased but remain above their long-run averages. Final data are due on 1 December for manufacturing and 3 December for services and the composite.

title: California widens Nvidia probe to criminal law, a bigger deal than Huang return talk
body: An open-ended state criminal investigation, on top of an SEC probe, adds a legal risk premium that's hard to price. That could cap Nvidia rebounds even as the broader market steadies. The stock's weight in major indices means headline risk here can spill into the Nasdaq and the wider AI trade, and into Asian chip names already under pressure. Investors may also start pricing a lower chance of Huang returning, which removes one potential upside catalyst that some had been counting on. The board's subpoena response and any disclosure in regulatory filings are the near-term flashpoints. Newswire cut: California's Nvidia probe now covers possible criminal breaches of state law over China chip sales and whether Nvidia or ex-CEO Jensen Huang misled the public, AG Rob Bonta said. The SEC is also investigating, raising the stakes for any Huang return. One-line wrap: The market has been arguing about whether Huang comes back, while California has been quietly building a case that could make that question irrelevant. Summary: California AG Rob Bonta says his Nvidia investigation covers potential criminal violations of state law. The probe examines whether Nvidia or Huang gave false information about chip sales to China, and whether investors were misled. It is preliminary, with no conclusions. Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena on 19 November, a week after Huang resigned. The SEC is also investigating, reportedly including whether Nvidia misled investors.

title: OCBC: AI rout becomes a growth shock as EM currencies take the dollar's strength

Carry trades funded in low-yielders are vulnerable to further unwinding if the AI sell-off resumes, which could add volatility to Asian currencies, especially those tied to chip exports. A clearer Fed pause signal, along the lines JPMorgan's Kelly expects, would be the main thing that could ease the pressure on EM. Any repeat of last week's forced selling in metals would support the "growth shock" reading. - The AI unwind has stopped being just a rates story, OCBC says, and emerging market currencies are paying for the dollar's resilience. Summary: OCBC strategists say the interest rate shock may have evolved into a growth shock, as AI de-risking hits equities, EM carry trades and metals. Concerns over the AI investment cycle have lowered stocks and US yields, shifting the pressure from the stronger dollar onto EM currencies. They expect the dollar to stay supported in the short term by hawkish Fed risk and tightening global financial conditions. In October, OCBC's Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong warned that a US-centric AI shock could hurt the dollar. By November they expected it to stay firm into 1H27. title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6775 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. --- Earlier: China cuts margin requirement to 80% in fresh market support push, but will it work? --- China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks.

title: The AI winners may not exist yet, J.P. Morgan warns, as mega-IPOs flood the market
body: J.P. Morgan's numbers push back on one popular explanation for the AI sell-off, that a flood of new shares is draining liquidity. That puts the focus back on valuations and earnings doubts as the real drivers. Strong household, foreign and buyback demand also suggests a deep pool of buyers if sentiment stabilises, which supports the buy-the-dip case. The point that much of the value creation now happens before listing is a caution for anyone chasing new AI listings, and it could weigh on post-IPO performance. --- Earlier: Goldman names 3 signals that could mark a bottom as the S&P 500 sits 12% below its record --- The AI listing boom is huge in dollar terms but small next to the market absorbing it, and J.P. Demand is growing faster than supply: households bought more than $800 billion of equities in the first half, foreign investors over $350 billion, and buybacks have topped $1.3 trillion. An estimated 85% to 95% of companies with more than $100 million in revenue remain private, and unicorns are worth about $8 trillion. The bank warned that the eventual AI winners may not exist yet.

title: SNB's Martin eyes second-round effects after inflation jumps to 1.5%, hike in view
body: Martin's focus on second-round effects is a hawkish signal, and it supports pricing for a December SNB hike. A tightening Swiss central bank alongside a hiking Fed changes the usual rate-differential story for the franc. Combined with strong safe-haven demand during the equity rout, that could keep the franc well bid, especially against the euro. That is the very currency risk Martin flagged, so the SNB may stay willing to lean against excessive franc strength even as it tightens. UBS shares remain exposed to headlines on the capital rules and any further talk of a headquarters move. --- Swiss inflation is still within target, but its speed has the SNB watching wages and prices closely, and a December hike now looks like a live option. Summary: SNB Vice Chairman Antoine Martin told Le Matin Dimanche the bank is paying particular attention to possible second-round inflation effects. Swiss annual inflation rose faster than expected to 1.5% in October from 1% in September, raising expectations of a December hike. The SNB targets 0% to 2%. Chairman Martin Schlegel had said the jump surprised the bank. Martin said the franc "very clearly" remains a safe haven and named exchange-rate swings as the SNB's main risk. He reiterated SNB support for requiring UBS to fully capitalise its foreign subsidiaries and said any headquarters move would be for UBS management to decide.

title: Gold sinks 9% in a week as margin calls and Fed hike bets override its haven role
body: Gold is currently trading as a funding asset, so its near-term direction depends more on equity volatility and leveraged positioning than on traditional safe-haven demand. A December Fed hike is close to fully priced, so further downside from rates alone may be limited. The bigger risk is another wave of liquidation if the AI sell-off deepens. Spot is now far below every major bank's year-end target, so forecast cuts could keep coming, which may weigh on sentiment even if outright selling slows. A sustained halt in equity losses is likely to be the first trigger for bargain hunting. --- Last week: Gold at $3,625: five forces behind the sell-off, and four reasons buyers haven't quit --- In this sell-off, gold isn't the shelter. It's one of the first things investors sell to cover losses elsewhere. Summary: Spot gold fell about 2.7% on Friday to around $3,525 an ounce, a 14-month low, and lost roughly 9% over the week, its worst week in eight months. title: Korea's market rescue fund is worth around $8 billion, but is 10.76 trillion won enough?
body: The fund's size makes it more of a confidence signal than a market mover, so traders are likely to watch how quickly and how visibly it is deployed, not just its headline value. If it is activated and the selling doesn't slow, pressure could build for a larger fund or for the outright short-selling curbs that authorities have so far avoided. Heavy foreign short positioning also leaves room for sharp short-covering rallies if sentiment turns, which could make Kospi swings even wider in both directions this week. title: Could Nvidia shareholders force Huang back? The 15% hurdle behind a long-shot idea
body: For now this is a watch item, not a trading catalyst. There's no filing, no coalition and a board that has firmly closed the door. If it did escalate into a formal fight, the leadership uncertainty would likely weigh on Nvidia shares in the near term, whatever the outcome, at a time when AI stocks are already under heavy pressure. Some investors would treat a credible path back for Huang as positive for strategic continuity, which is why any SEC filings showing coordinated holders would draw immediate attention. The export compliance review is still the more important driver for the stock. --- A shareholder revolt to bring Huang back makes a good headline, but with no filing, a 15% threshold and a board that has said no, it's one to watch, not one to bet on. Summary: Activist investor Bill Ackman says Huang's backers could seek a special shareholder meeting and that the threat of a vote might sway the board. He doesn't plan to get involved. No formal campaign, filing or special meeting request has been reported. Nvidia's bylaws require holders with 15% of voting power, held for a year, to call a special meeting. Huang owns about 3.6%. Board chair Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress say the board won't reinstate Huang. Pressure is coming from an open letter, some investors, President Trump and, as of Sunday, a softer stance from Treasury Secretary Bessent.

title: Bessent leaves door open to Huang return at Nvidia, a week after urging an outside CEO
body: Removing Washington's apparent veto on Huang lowers one source of leadership uncertainty at the world's most important AI chipmaker, which could ease some of the pressure on Nvidia after last week's slide. The bigger regulatory overhang is still there, though. Any finding of export-control breaches could bring penalties or tighter limits on China-linked sales, which would hit revenue expectations directly. Traders are likely to treat the board's compliance response as a binary event for the stock and for AI sentiment more broadly. A clean answer would also strengthen the case for a Huang return. --- Earlier: US equity rout: Bessent cautions Fed against overtightening, before its December decision --- A week ago Bessent wanted an outsider running Nvidia. Now the door is open for Huang, as long as the compliance answers hold up. Summary: On CBS on Sunday, Bessent declined to rule out Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO, saying it depends on "where the buck stops." On Fox News on 15 November, he had called for a shake-up and an outside successor, and gave Nvidia 10 days to answer compliance questions. He said he assumed Huang didn't know a woman linked to the scandal was an alleged spy, and said his "culture of non-compliance" remark described a possibility. body: EUR/USD 1.1060 (EUR 519.34 mn) 1.1030 (EUR 499.54 mn) 1.1010 (EUR 432.56 mn) 1.0950 (EUR 774.00 mn) USD/JPY 159.25 (US$ 1.43 bn) 158.00 (US$ 1.02 bn) GBP/USD 1.3425 (GBP 1.25 bn) 1.3240 (GBP 2.30 bn) USD/CHF 0.8425 (US$ 393.38 mn) 0.8150 (US$ 600.00 mn) USD/CAD 1.4300 (US$ 437.93 mn) AUD/USD 0.6735 (AUD 380.92 mn) 0.6675 (AUD 384.04 mn) 0.6640 (AUD 388.32 mn) NZD/USD 0.5540 (NZD 974.43 mn) EUR/GBP 0.8370 (EUR 280.58 mn) What are FX option expiries? The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts. When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET). Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on). As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes.

title: Crypto crime: Fusionist's ACE bridge emptied of $3.7 million as traders follow a $2 million exploit
body: ACE fell to about $0.0001 on BNB Chain but still traded around $0.04 on centralised exchanges, and traders exploited that gap until the bridge ran dry. The drained 53.7 million tokens are almost half of the roughly 116 million ACE in circulation before the attack. They now sit in 24 wallets, and one wallet alone holds 26.1 million, so the main near-term risk is selling pressure on exchange-listed ACE. Gate is moving its ACE perpetuals to reduce-only and then delisting them, which leaves one fewer place to hedge. The incident is too small to affect BTC, ETH, crypto equities or ETF flows. Its main significance is for how the market prices bridge risk in small-cap gaming tokens. --- One abused minter role let a hacker walk off with $2 million, and a crowd of opportunists took the next $3.7 million before the bridge ran out of tokens. Summary: On Sunday an attacker used privileged minter access on Fusionist's bridge to create unbacked ACE on BNB Chain, starting with 3.5 million tokens and finishing with a single mint of 10 quintillion. The tokens were sold as they were minted for about 1,150 ETH, roughly $2 million. The proceeds were moved to Ethereum and sent into Tornado Cash. Traders bought the cheap BNB Chain ACE and redeemed it through the bridge, taking about 53.7 million real ACE (about $3.7 million) across 24 addresses and leaving 0.08 ACE behind. One wallet turned about $50 into roughly $17,670 in under 20 minutes.

title: Economic and event calendar in Asia Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Singapore and Japan
body: Singapore Q3 GDP: 0000 GMT / 1900 US Eastern Singapore starts the Asian data day with third-quarter GDP. Economists expect growth of 1.3% quarter on quarter, up from 1.1% in the previous reading. On a year-on-year basis, they expect 5.6% against 5.4% before. If the figures land on forecast, they will confirm that the city-state's economy gained speed through the third quarter, at a strong annual pace for a mature, trade-dependent economy. Singapore is often read as a bellwether for regional trade, so a strong print would point to steady demand across Asia's export supply chains. That matters for the region's manufacturing story heading into the end of the year. A beat on the year-on-year number would add to the picture of resilient regional activity. A miss would raise questions about how long that momentum can last. Watch also for any change to official full-year growth expectations, which can move the Singapore dollar and local rates. The data will also feed into the Monetary Authority of Singapore's next policy review. MAS has scheduled its January 2027 statement for release no later than 29 January, after its last decision on 14 October. Unlike most central banks, MAS does not set an interest rate. It runs monetary policy through the exchange rate, adjusting the slope, width and centre of the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER) policy band, and since 2024 it has issued decisions four times a year, in January, April, July and October.

title: Silver sets the technical boundaries in the short term for traders
body: Silver is trading higher today after falling to its lowest level since September 2025 on Friday. The rebound took the price from $40.75 to a session high of $44.25, a gain of about 8.6% from Friday's low. The move ran into sellers at the 100-hour moving average, however, and the price has since rotated lower. The broader trend has been lower since September. Silver stalled at $67.30 on September 26 and moved back below its 100-day moving average, which was at $66.59 at the time. From there, the price stepped lower. The November 10 swing high at $53.72 marked the start of the latest leg down, which took silver to $40.75 on Friday. Buyers leaned against trendline support. Friday's low tested the downward-sloping trendline drawn through the October 14 and October 30 lows. Sellers could not extend the move below that line, giving buyers a level to lean against. A break below the line would have given those buyers a reason to get out quickly. With support holding, silver had room to rebound as gold moved higher and broader risk sentiment improved. The 100-hour moving average is the barometer on the topside. At today's high near $44.25, silver tested its 100-hour moving average and turned lower. That gives sellers a level to lean against as well. As long as the price stays below that moving average, the rebound remains corrective within the broader downtrend. A move above it that can hold would give buyers their first sign that the short-term bias is shifting in their favor.

title: Crude oil settles at $80.17. Trades at its lowest level since August 26.
body: WTI crude oil fell nearly 4% Monday, trading near $80.20 a barrel around settlement after reaching an intraday low of $79.95. The selloff extends a slide that had already pushed crude to three straight weekly declines. So what gave sellers the upper hand today? Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened. Libya's National Oil Corporation told Reuters that crude had begun flowing into storage tanks at Zawiya. The restart adds to supply availability at a time when traders are already watching for a surplus. The market is looking ahead to more supply in 2027. The October rebound in Middle Eastern exports left more crude on tankers, and JPMorgan expects additional production from the Middle East outside Iran and from the Americas to contribute to a surplus next year. The bank sees oil futures in the high $70s in the first half of 2027. A stronger dollar added a headwind. The dollar rallied alongside the Nvidia-led rebound in stocks. That makes dollar-priced crude more expensive for buyers using other currencies and added pressure to a market already selling off on supply news. The telling part of today's move is that crude fell even after reports of fresh attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz. Traders put more weight on the barrels coming back into the market and the prospect of more supply next year. The next policy event is the November 29 OPEC+ meeting, when producers are due to discuss 2027 output. For traders, $80 is the immediate barometer. Trade above is more bullish.

title: The EURUSD is moving below a retracement target and to the lowest level since April 2025
body: EURUSD has extended to a new low for the day, moving back below the swing area between 1.09041 and 1.09499. In the process, the price also broke below the 61.8% retracement of the move up from the January 2025 low to the January 2026 high. That retracement comes in at 1.09048, just seven-tenths of a pip above the bottom of the swing area. That puts two technical levels in nearly the same spot. The 1.09041 to 1.09048 area is now the first barometer for buyers and sellers. Stay below it, and the bearish bias remains intact. If the price moves back above that pocket and holds, the immediate downside pressure eases and buyers get room to work back through the swing area. They would still need to get and stay above 1.09499 to take more control. What's next on the downside? The session low at 1.08880 is the first level sellers need to get through to extend the move. Below that, there's little obvious support on the daily chart until the late-March 2025 low near 1.07337. That makes 1.07337 the next major downside target if sellers can keep the pressure on. Education. How to use a broken level to define risk When a swing level and a retracement sit this close together, watch how the price behaves around both on a retest. Here, a bounce that stalls near 1.09041 to 1.09048 would show that sellers are defending former support as resistance. A move back above both levels that holds would raise the risk of a failed break and give sellers a reason to reassess.

title: Gold futures rebounded nearly 4% from a 14-month low.
body: Gold futures rallied nearly 4% to $3,655 on Monday, rebounding from a 14-month closing low in the previous session. The move followed a broad shift in market sentiment sparked by strength in equities and evolving artificial intelligence and semiconductor news, including developments surrounding Nvidia's leadership. That positive momentum carried across the metals complex, lifting silver and copper alongside gold. Despite the sharp start-of-week bounce, gold remains well below where it opened the prior week after a 9% weekly drawdown, its largest percentage decline in eight months. Market participants are watching to see whether the recovery holds or proves to be a short-term reaction to equity sentiment.

title: Tech rally lifts U.S. equities.
body: U.S. equities surged in morning trading, led by Nasdaq futures, alongside gains in metals and cryptocurrencies. Bob Iaccino breaks down the mixed manufacturing PMI data and the tech-driven rally, highlighting Nvidia's 31% jump following the board's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang. Iaccino also previews upcoming consumer confidence data, evaluating the potential impact of midterm elections and falling gas prices on consumer sentiment. Plus, a look ahead to comments from the Fed's John Williams, 2-Year and 5-Year Treasury note auctions, and the schedule for corporate earnings and global economic data.

title: Euro FX futures fell below 1.09 to lowest since April.
body: Euro FX futures declined sharply to start the week, sliding from a session high near 1.10 to dip below 1.09 before closing around that level. The intraday move below 1.09 marked the lowest print since April, though modest buying emerged off the lows. Renewed expectations for Federal Reserve tightening supported the U.S. dollar, adding downward pressure on the euro. As prices pressed toward year-to-date lows, implied volatility tracked by the CVOL index firmed higher. Positioning data from last week, prior to Monday's selloff, also showed speculators adding to net short positions, bringing bearish positioning to its highest level in more than 10 years.

title: 10-Year T-Note futures held firm as yields dipped to 4.92%.
body: 10-Year T-Note futures held steady to start the week as the 10-Year Treasury yield navigated a choppy session around 4.94% before closing down 2 bps at 4.92%. While risk assets staged a broad recovery following last week's selloff, the bond market retained much of its recent flight-to-quality bid, signaling a measured wait-and-see posture. Alongside lower yields, interest rate volatility tracked by the CVOL index also moved lower even as equities and other risk assets rebounded. Attention now turns to Tuesday's economic calendar, which features the ADP employment report, the Philadelphia Fed non-manufacturing index and consumer confidence, followed later in the session by 2-Year floating rate note and 5-Year Treasury note auctions.

title: WTI Crude Oil futures fell below $80 to 3-month lows.
body: WTI Crude Oil futures faced heavy selling pressure on Monday, dipping to an intraday low of $79.88 before trading near $80.15, marking three-month lows and the first move below $80 in several months. The three-week pullback follows a late-October multi-month high above $100 and reflects improving global supply and demand balance, with increased production and distribution flowing from the Middle East. Weakness extended across the broader energy complex, weighing on RBOB Gasoline, heating oil and Natural Gas futures. After approaching the top of its range late last week, the Jan Natural Gas futures contract fell about 6% to roughly $3.52 as positions rolled into January.

title: E-mini S&P 500 futures jumped 350 points on AI optimism.
body: E-mini S&P 500 futures rallied nearly 5% to start the week, climbing 350 points toward 7,270 heading into the close. Driven by AI optimism and broader strength across risk assets, the rebound reversed last week's drop below 7,000, which marked the index's first close under that level since April. As equity indices moved sharply higher, implied volatility softened after spiking on Friday, though it held off session lows. Looking ahead to Tuesday's calendar, market participants await early ADP employment data, the Philadelphia nonmanufacturing index, consumer confidence figures and additional corporate earnings, with no Federal Reserve speakers scheduled.

title: Live Cattle futures rose on cash; Lean Hog futures hit lows.
body: Livestock markets saw mixed trading as Live Cattle futures gapped higher following Friday's report and stronger Midwest cash prices up to $220. Feb Live Cattle futures climbed $2.20 to $229.90, Apr reached $223 and Dec hit $225.37, with CVOL at 16.2%. Feeder Cattle futures traded firm after Oct. placements fell to their lowest level since 1996; Jan Feeder Cattle futures rose $3.88 to $339.30 and Mar reached $335.75 before paring gains, with CVOL at 17.7%. Lean Hog futures moved lower as weak export sales pushed prices to new contract lows. Feb Lean Hog futures fell 75 cents to $56.22, Dec dropped to $51.70 and Apr reached $63.22—more than $30 below the March high—while CVOL stood at 36%.

title: Soybean futures rose on U.S. demand; Wheat held near lows.
body: Grain markets saw mixed action as Soybean futures rose on stronger U.S. demand while a rapidly developing Brazilian crop limited gains. Jan Soybean futures climbed 14 1/4 cents to 1235'0 before pulling back 10 cents, and Mar reached 1238'6, with option open interest reaching 121,000 and CVOL at 15%. Corn futures traded mixed as lagging inspections and shipments weighed on prices; Mar held an eight-cent range near 448'0, Dec settled around 433'0 and corn CVOL stood at 17.8%. Wheat futures held steady near recent lows as managed money added to short positions amid ample global supplies and Black Sea logistics issues.
